value.desc: Ten minutes into meeting someone, you already know who they are. Months later, everyone else catches up to what you saw in the first handshake.
When everyone at the table is talking around the problem, you're the one who names it. People save their hardest questions for you because you won't dress up the answer.
The day everything breaks is the day you're calmest. While others freeze, you're already cutting the problem into pieces that can be solved.
Strangers get the edge. The few people you've let past it get someone who shows up at 2 AM without being asked, every time.
You take longer to call something done, and it shows. What leaves your hands doesn't come back for fixing.
